# Paying down a USD payable from a CAD bank, written by hand.
#
# The A/P split is a debit — it reduces what is owed — and that is money the
# book has sent, not currency it holds. A prepayment to a vendor is a debit on
# the same account and *is* currency the book has a claim on, so direction
# alone cannot tell them apart: what does is the lot. A settlement belongs to
# the bill it settles; a prepayment belongs to nothing yet.
#
# What this fixture produces: `fx-balances` finds no cost basis at all. A rule
# that counted either direction on a payable opened a 100.00 USD basis here,
# offering currency that had already left the book.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_foreign_currency_cost_basis.py.
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Liabilities
	type: Liability
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Liabilities:Accounts Payable USD
	type: Accounts Payable
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"

2026-02-01 * "Pay down the USD payable"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Liabilities:Accounts Payable USD 100.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1.40"
		value: "140.00"
	Assets:Bank -140.00 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		share_price: "1"
		value: "-140.00"
